title: Turning professional in 1909 and the New Orleans bandleaders
summary: Garland became professional in 1909, liked by bandleaders Perez, Dusen, Dawson and Robichaux, and played with the Eagle, Crescent, Imperial and Peerless bands.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I heard a demonstration earlier, and the next time we get together we're going to tape some of your own style. We're going to hear the Closer Walk on tape, which is great. So you then -- you were a professional musician at what age, Tootie? How old were you when you became a professional?
I got to be a professional in -- really,
Because all those bandleaders, they all liked me. There was something about it, I was friendly with all of them.
I'd take Manuel Perez. Dusen. Frankie Dawson.

Robichaux. They all -- they used to call me The Kid. "Let's get The Kid." All them bass players was coming over to me and stick me up on that stand, you understand, to play. And I played, and they'd shake their heads. I'm growing fast. And I was growing fast, if I have to say it myself. Done fine with the Eagle Band, I done fine with the Crescent Band -- Jack Corey's band, that is.
Done fine with the Imperial Band. And done fine with Bab Frank, the Peerless Band.
Right. Bab Frank was the piccolo player. Right?
The piccolo player. Yeah. Buddy Red.
